Chapter 01—Today

Plan the day.

Today puts the next event first, then your tasks and rituals. Add a task or check in on a ritual without opening another page.

  1. A brief, when you want one.

    Tap Brief for what is next, what is open, the rituals kept, and today’s focus, with Ask Daymark one tap away.

  2. The forecast beside the plans.

    The selected city’s Apple Weather forecast appears above tasks and events for the day.

  3. See the day in hours.

    Open the day to see events laid out in time, and step through the week from the strip above.

  4. Find a day in the month.

    Days with events carry a mark. Tap one to open it.

  5. Every task in one list.

    Open tasks are grouped by day. Finished ones fold away under Done.

  6. Give a task its time.

    Block time for a task with a start and a length. It lands in the daybook, and on your Apple calendar once you import a writable one.

Chapter 02—Rituals

Keep a practice.

Set a daily, weekday, or weekly rhythm, then review check-ins across the week.

  1. Check in across the week.

    Use daily, weekday, or weekly cadences. Check in from Today or from the Rituals page.

    Check in from Today or from the Rituals page.

Chapter 03—Focus

Protect your attention.

Give one task a protected block of time, then see where today’s focus went.

  1. One dial, one task.

    Run a Pomodoro with focus, short rest, and long rest, or pick a 25, 50, or 90 minute session.

  2. Timers and countdowns.

    Keep reusable timers for the things you do often, and count down to the dates ahead.

  3. See where the time went.

    Focus history keeps the last seven days and today’s sessions in one ledger.

  4. Focus comes with you.

    A running session stays in view while you move to another page.

Swipe to explore · 1 of 4

Chapter 04—Review

Review what mattered.

Weekly Review gathers completed tasks, focus sessions, and ritual check-ins from the week you recorded.

  1. A week you can see.

    Tasks done, focus minutes, and rituals kept come together beside three prompts: what mattered, what got in the way, and one change for next week.

Chapter 05—Shelf

Keep what deserves to stay.

Notes, links, and images in one place. Share from another app and it lands on the Shelf the next time you open Daymark.

  1. Filter by kind or tag.

    Pin what should stay on top, and tag entries so they are easy to gather again.

  2. A note, ready to return to.

    Copy it, share it, edit it, or move it to Recently deleted. Entries can be restored there for 30 days.

  3. Find anything in the daybook.

    Search tasks, events, Shelf entries, rituals, and weekly reviews. Spotlight indexing is optional.

Swipe to explore · 1 of 3

Chapter 06—Ask

Ask about your day.

Ask Daymark answers from your daybook and makes typed, explainable changes. It works offline, with or without the optional model.

  1. A brief from the day you have.

    Ask for the day’s shape and get an answer from the events, tasks, rituals, focus, and weather already in Daymark.

  2. From phrase to typed action.

    With the optional Gemma 4 model, a loose sentence can produce a typed action and reviewable receipt. Daymark validates and writes the change.

  3. Grounded by default.

    In Daybook mode, answers come from your actual day, and each reply is tagged with the mode that wrote it.

  4. Open conversation, on request.

    Switch to Open chat for general questions. Web search is off unless you turn it on.

Swipe to explore · 1 of 4

Chapter 07—Settings

Yours to set.

Daymark starts empty and stays quiet until you ask for more.

  1. It starts empty.

    A fresh install holds nothing of yours. Explore a sample day to see the loop, then choose Start fresh to clear it.

  2. Choose the paper.

    Pick a paper tone and an accent, or let Daylight move the page with the sun.

  3. Reminders you opt into.

    A morning brief, due tasks, ritual nudges, and event alerts. Each one is off until you turn it on.

  4. Your calendar, live.

    Connect Apple Calendar and Reminders, then choose the calendars and lists Daymark reads. Edits save back to those accounts.

  5. Keep a copy, or start again.

    Import or export tasks, events, and Shelf entries. Spotlight is optional. Erase Daymark data has its own confirmation.

Private by default. Clear about the exceptions.

Daymark has no account, analytics, cloud sync, or remote AI service. A few optional connections belong to features you choose to use.

Your daybookStored in Daymark on this device.

Web searchOff by default. Only your question is sent when you search.

Calendar and RemindersUses the system accounts and lists you select.

Weather and linksConnect to providers only when those features are used.
